ctx.x: Well, what happened? What was Marshall Sterns doing for tap dancers?

Well, what he was going to do, he was going to give them like a world tour, which we call monarchy -- rather I calls it monarchy, when one is fortunate to go around the world and meet all the, you know, the populations, you see. And eventually he was going to make films. He was going to make movies, you know. And he was going to feature like type-cast tap dancing, you see, which I think there's going to be one -- someone, a young film maker like is coming in the future here now -- George C. Nurenberg. He's going…

young film maker. I don't know whether he'll bring it over, you know, but he may do it. I guess I'm going to try to help as much as I can about tap dancing as long as I'm in it. I mean that's what Chuckles would have wanted. And when everybody that I know -- my aunt and everybody -- I mean the family, especially John Bubbles, you see. And, you know. And Bill Bojangles Robinson, you know. Because I used to tell stories, Little like traveling experiences, you know.
